a6-ss5: Since they're already overstimulated, it helps to clear out the crowd and stop any arguing. While it's natural for people who are overstimulated to start pacing or exercising to "burn it off," the problem is that creates more body heat, and it raises the risk of their muscles breaking down into the blood, which hurts the kidneys (rhabdomyolysis). But if they feel a strong urge to keep moving (akathisia), I'd have them do some tapping (the Emotional Freedom Technique, fingers tapping the head), which can soothe that urge without the over-activity risk.
a6-ss7b: The ER doctors will want to know exactly what they took, so before the ambulance comes, I'd gather their pill bottles and packages. I'd also jot down how much of each they took and when, street drugs and supplements included. And if they have a seizure before the ambulance gets there, I'd do the first aid in Active Seizure above, and keep track of how their breathing is doing afterward, as that's one of the main indicators of how dangerous the seizure is, according to the CDC.
a6-ss8: While you wait, you might think of niacin, which this guide uses for ending a trip, but it's actually unsafe with serotonin syndrome, since at the doses used to end a trip it can cause flushing, dizziness and low blood pressure (NIH). DMSO, though, seems to help prevent seizures, so if there's any sign of an overdose, I'd have them smell it, or rub a little on a clean patch of skin (add 30% water if it makes the skin itch), then slowly use more as long as it seems to help. I'd also leave out this guide's Syrian rue oil for now: made at home it has almost none of the harmala alkaloids, but I couldn't find any research on it with MDMA, so it could help or harm here. Magnesium chloride is the other one I'd use, since many people with serotonin syndrome run low on magnesium (a nursing review). If they're fully alert and able to swallow, I'd give it by mouth, especially with MDMA-related jaw tension or muscle activity (the amounts are in MDMA: Magnesium Alarm, above). Topical magnesium chloride if they're not able to swallow, or Epsom salt if that's all you have, though Epsom salt gets through the skin less well.
